note: Graded build prompts for scripts/benchmark.py. Tiers run in order and get harder. Each prompt is a single build request against a fresh project, written the way someone would actually type it, not tuned to make the model succeed. 'expect' lists what a human should look for when reviewing the finished app; the harness cannot judge these, so they are printed as a review checklist next to the machine result.

cases.title: Personal reading list
cases.prompt: Build a reading list. Each book has a title, author, and a status of want to read, reading, or finished. I want to add a book, change its status, and delete it. Show the list grouped by status with a count next to each group. Store everything in PostgreSQL with a migration, and add backend tests.
expect: Adding a book persists across a page reload
Status can be changed without retyping the book
Counts match the number of rows in each group

cases.title: Daily habit tracker
cases.prompt: Build a habit tracker. I can create habits and tick each one off per day. Show the last 7 days as a grid with the habits down the side and the days across the top, and show the current streak for each habit. Store it in PostgreSQL with a migration, and add backend tests for the streak calculation.
expect: Ticking a day persists and the grid reflects it
Streak resets correctly after a missed day
The grid is readable at phone width

cases.title: Client tracker with invoices
cases.prompt: Build a client tracker on top of the existing accounts app. Each signed-in user has their own clients, and each client has invoices with an amount, issue date, due date, and a paid or unpaid status. I want a client list showing their outstanding total, a page per client listing its invoices, and a way to mark an invoice paid. Only the owner may see or change their own clients and invoices. Add a migration and backend tests covering ownership. Keep every existing account, billing, role and operations screen working.
expect: A second account cannot see the first account's clients
Existing sign-in, roles and billing screens still work

cases.title: Filtered list with CSV export
cases.prompt: Add a searchable, filterable table of the current user's notes, with a text search, a date range filter, and a button that downloads the filtered rows as a CSV. The CSV must contain only the signed-in user's own rows. Add backend tests that prove the export respects both the filter and record ownership.
expect: The downloaded CSV matches what the filtered table shows
A second account's rows never appear in the export
Search and date filter combine rather than replace each other

cases.title: Booking with availability rules
cases.prompt: Build a room booking feature. An admin defines rooms and their opening hours per weekday. A member books a room for a time slot. Two bookings for the same room must never overlap, and a booking outside the room's opening hours must be refused with a clear message. Show a day view per room. Enforce all of this on the server, not just in the interface. Add a migration and backend tests for the overlap and opening-hours rules, including two bookings submitted at the same time.
expect: Concurrent identical bookings produce exactly one booking
The overlap rule is enforced in the API, not only the UI
Only an admin can change rooms or opening hours

cases.title: Threaded comments with moderation
cases.prompt: Add comments to the notes. Comments can reply to other comments, nested up to three levels. An author can edit or delete their own comment; an admin can delete any comment. A deleted comment that has replies keeps its place in the thread and shows as removed. Add a migration and backend tests covering the nesting limit, the edit and delete permissions, and the removed-with-replies case.
expect: A member cannot edit or delete another member's comment
Deleting a parent does not orphan or hide its replies
The nesting limit is enforced server-side
